subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should distinct ACP child sessions remain parallel by default while ACPX launch readiness is fixed, or should OpenClaw add an explicit concurrency gate for ACPX spawns?
rationale: Current code and tests intentionally allow different ACP sessions to run in parallel, so changing that default is a product/runtime-boundary decision rather than a mechanical bug fix without live proof.

options.title: Reproduce then fix the owner boundary
options.body: Run current ACPX/Claude two-spawn proof first, then repair ACPX launch readiness or OpenClaw wrapper startup only where the failure is confirmed, preserving default parallelism.

options.title: Add an explicit ACPX launch gate
options.body: If maintainers decide ACPX cannot safely initialize distinct child sessions concurrently, add a narrow documented gate or cap with upgrade/user-visible behavior proof.

options.title: Close after clean live proof
options.body: If current main and latest stable both pass the rapid two-spawn ACPX/Claude smoke with both children producing assistant output, close this as no longer reproducible and cite the proof.

recommendation.title: Reproduce then fix the owner boundary
recommendation.body: Run current ACPX/Claude two-spawn proof first, then repair ACPX launch readiness or OpenClaw wrapper startup only where the failure is confirmed, preserving default parallelism.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the ACP thread-bound agent control plane and later owned the ACPX runtime-library boundary that this decision crosses.
